conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: A ships fully static, semantic HTML (role=banner, role=search, labeled inputs, visually-hidden legend heading) so the release notes are present and readable even if JS fails, while B's entire page — including the dedicated config-reference route — is an empty <main id="app"> shell rendered only by app.js, a real resilience gap for a CI-adjacent tool. A's copy-to-clipboard handler checks whether the fallback execCommand actually succeeded and shows an honest failure message; B's fallback path always displays 'Copied' regardless of outcome. B also has a reproducible mobile CSS bug (.toolbar switches to flex-direction:column at max-width:480px while .search keeps flex: 1 1 14rem, so the 14rem flex-basis is applied along the now-vertical axis) that inserts a large blank gap before the breaking-change content on the 390px viewport, visible in three separate evidence captures. B does have a genuinely stronger config-reference destination (a real page that honestly discloses no migration guide URL was supplied, versus A's static in-page placeholder) and a clearer job-framing sentence, but these gains are outweighed by A's stronger resilience, honesty, and mobile correctness.
suspected_unblinding: none — both source/README.md files are generic static-site starter boilerplate; no naming, comments, or metadata pointed to a particular builder or treatment.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The changelog and the config-reference page are both empty HTML shells (<main id="app"></main>) with all content generated client-side by app.js. If JS fails to load or execute, the page renders nothing at all — no release notes, no breaking-change warning.

findings.label: B
findings.description: On the 390px viewport, .toolbar sets flex-direction: column while its child .search keeps flex: 1 1 14rem from the desktop rule; in a column flex context that 14rem flex-basis applies to height, not width, forcing the search control to occupy ~224px and leaving a large blank gap before the breaking-change content starts.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The copy-to-clipboard fallback (document.execCommand("copy")) does not check its boolean return value — the button always shows 'Copied' even when the fallback copy silently failed.

findings.label: A
findings.description: In two evidence captures (interaction-01, state-01), the sticky topbar renders a second time mid-page, overlapping the breaking-change callout. This is consistent with a known Chromium/Playwright interaction between position: sticky and full-page screenshot capture rather than necessarily a real scrolling-browser defect, but it is the only evidence supplied and is confusing as presented.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The five note types are differentiated only by a label chip and a 4px left-border color; the breaking note gets no extra visual weight (background tint, size) versus the other four, slightly undercutting the 'identify the breaking change in one scan' requirement compared to A's shaded, callout-boxed breaking treatment.
